articles.title: CoGaussian: Open-Vocabulary Gaussian-based Collaborative 3D Scene Understanding
articles.summary: Collaborative perception enables agents to retrieve the scene semantics and geometry beyond the field of view of any individual agent. This broader scene understanding enhances transportation safety and improves efficiency in multi-robot systems. However, existing collaborative semantic occupancy methods rely on dense 3D voxel annotations and are limited to recognizing objects within a predefined set of semantic classes. To overcome these limitations, we present CoGaussian, an open-vocabulary Gaussian-based collaborative semantic occupancy prediction framework. CoGaussian represents a scene as a set of foundation model-aligned sparse 3D Gaussians, which serve as a compact representation for communicating and fusing geometric and semantic information across multiple agents. On the Semantic-OPV2V benchmark, our method outperforms existing open-vocabulary single-agent approaches, highlighting the effectiveness of open-vocabulary collaborative scene understanding.

articles.title: Architectural Deep-Dive: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
articles.summary: Decoupling Perception and Compute: How Persistent Multimodal Memory Fixes Agentic Tool Bottlenecks Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous visual agents tasked with analyzing technical schematics, executing system telemetry diagnostics, and verifying physical mockups. However, in production environments, a familiar wall is encountered: inference-time scaling does not solve context rot. When agents invoke diagnostic tools, search APIs, or visual crops, the naive design pattern is to inject the raw multi-megabyte payloads directly back into the conversation context window. This creates severe token inflation, increases quadratic self-attention latency, and induces hallucinations during arithmetic reasoning over heterogeneous observations. The paper OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory (arXiv:2610.26860) details a concrete architectural solution that eliminates this bottleneck. articles.title: Mistral AI Releases Timestral: A 209M Forecasting Model Family That Outperforms Google’s TimesFM-3
articles.summary: Mistral released Timestral, a time series foundation model family from 5M to 209M parameters. The 209M model leads GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench among zero-shot models and runs on CPU.
